chunks: 1527 - Muḥammad ibn Muslim and Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah narrated from Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbdillāh, peace be upon them, who said:

"When an eclipse or some of these signs occurs, perform it so long as you do not fear that the time of the obligatory prayer will pass. But if you fear that, then begin with the obligatory prayer and cut short what you were engaged in of Salat al-Kusuf. Then when you have finished the obligatory prayer, return to where you had stopped and count what has already passed."

key_terms.وَقْتُ ٱلْفَرِيضَةِ: the appointed time of the obligatory prayer
key_terms.وَٱحْتَسِبْ بِمَا مَضَىٰ: count what has already been performed
key_terms.ٱلْآيَاتِ: signs such as extraordinary celestial or natural events
key_terms.ٱلْكُسُوفُ: the eclipse requiring the special prayer

ai.seo_question: What should be done if the time of an obligatory prayer begins while performing Salat al-Kusuf?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the order between Salat al-Kusuf and an obligatory prayer when their times overlap. It instructs that the obligatory prayer takes priority if its time is feared to lapse, and that one may then resume Salat al-Kusuf from where it was interrupted.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1527 - Muhammad ibn Muslim and Burayd ibn Muawiya narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) and Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:

"When an eclipse or any of these celestial signs occurs, perform the prayer (Salat al-Kusuf) as long as you do not fear missing the time of an obligatory prayer. If you fear that the time of the obligatory prayer will pass, then begin with the obligatory prayer and interrupt your Salat al-Kusuf. Once you have completed the obligatory prayer, return to where you left off in the Salat al-Kusuf and continue from there, counting what you have already performed."
